unit._previous_w2_81: Literal tail: `Tests: 1032 passed, 1032 total`, `Test Suites: 49 passed, 49 total`, jest exit 0, on the W2-81 branch (feature+trash-reconcile) from origin/main 45899ed. 1022 -> 1032 is +10, all in trashDay.test.ts, pinning the reconciliation contract between the shared completion and the device's SharedPreferences ack. 🔴 THE FINDING, AND IT INVERTS THE BRIEF'S OWN SUGGESTED ANSWER: "server wins" IS THE WRONG RULE. The server is authoritative for CLEARED and for nothing else; absence of a server record is NEVER evidence that nobody did it. A server-authoritative reading would overwrite the acknowledgement of any member who tapped OK while offline — which is EVERY member today, since nothing stamps a familyId — and show them the takeover again, the same nagging failure the dated ack exists to prevent, arriving from the other side. 🔑 SO THE RULE IS A UNION, NOT A PRECEDENCE: cleared if EITHER source says cleared, because both are POSITIVE evidence and neither one's silence is evidence of the negative. That is implementable without judgement, and it makes the un-clear failure STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE — there is no input in which a local value causes a server completion to be ignored — rather than merely discouraged. 📌 AND THE SERVER CANNOT BE MADE TO FORGET, VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, which is what makes the union safe: families/{familyId}/trashDay/{key} is `allow write: if false` to every client; the ONLY writer is completeTrashDay (index.ts:3832); planTrashDayCompletion is idempotent and returns the EXISTING completion rather than overwriting; and NO delete path exists anywhere in functions/. An un-clear has no server-side mechanism to travel through at all. ⚠️ WHICH CLOCK: NEITHER, BY CONSTRUCTION. The bin date is a LOCAL calendar date about a physical event (see BIN_DATE_MAX_SKEW_DAYS), so keys are compared as OPAQUE STRINGS and no instant is ever derived from one. Parsing a key to a timestamp is exactly how a comparison acquires a timezone it should not have, and this module has BOTH a UTC helper and a local key in scope — the precise confusion that produced the W2-80 anchor bug. A test feeds `${TODAY}T00:00:00Z` and asserts it does NOT match. 📌 A STALE LOCAL ACK IS HARMLESS AND THE REASON IS DERIVED, NOT TRUSTED: nextBinDate (trash_day_reminder.dart) returns TODAY when today is bin day and otherwise a FUTURE date — it never returns a past one — so an ack for a bygone date cannot match the bin date in question and no expiry rule is needed. ⚠️ THE COROLLARY IS A REAL LOSS AND IS NOT PAPERED OVER: a device offline past its bin day cannot sync that day's ack, because the +/-2 day skew window refuses it. CORRECT for clearing (the takeover has already moved on) but the record of WHO took the bins out is lost for that day. The window is exactly sufficient for acks that can still matter — the takeover opens the night before, so a live ack is at most a day out, plus one for any real UTC offset — and deliberately insufficient for those that cannot. THREE CONTROLS, each type-safe, each grepped back before undoing, and 🔑 THE FIRST TWO PROVE THE ASYMMETRY BECAUSE NEITHER ALONE CATCHES BOTH FAILURES: (1) local precedence over the server -> 1 red, 'server cleared, device holds a STALE ack for another day' — and note the 'device knows NOTHING' test stayed GREEN under it, because a null local ack falls through to the server, which is exactly why the sharper stale-ack fixture earns its place; (2) `cleared: serverSaysCleared` alone, the obvious-but-wrong rule -> 1 red, the CONTROL 'an ordinary same-day ack from the ONLY device still clears'; (3) the server date scoping dropped -> 1 red, 'a completion for ANOTHER day does not clear this one'. 📌 SCOPE: reconcileTrashDay is a NORMATIVE SPECIFICATION, not a callable the client invokes — Dart cannot call it. W1 ports the rule. It lives beside the writer it reconciles with so a change to one shows up as a red test on the other rather than as drift between a doc and an implementation. A free-Pro vector with a longer fuse than the invite one closed in W2-83. Every departure now revokes IN THE SAME TRANSACTION as the roster write; a revoke that is a second step is one a crash skips. 🔴 THE OWNER LEAVING DISSOLVES THE FAMILY — my reading, and the argument is that THE SUBSCRIPTION IS THE FAMILY.
